ILOCOS NORTE, KOREA TRAVEL TRADE STRENGTHEN TOURISM AND BUSINESS LINKAGES

The Province of Ilocos Norte and South Korean travel industry stakeholders are strengthening tourism and business linkages through the Ilocos Norte–Korea Tourism Business Meeting last, August 26, at the Plaza Del Norte Function Hall.The meeting is part of the Korea Travel Trade Familiarization Tour, which brings Korean travel trade representatives to Ilocos Norte from August 24 to 27, 2026. The activity builds on the Province’s Trade and Tourism Mission to South Korea in November 2025, led by the Department of Tourism (DOT) Region 1.Representatives from the DOT–Korea, DOT Region 1, Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte (PGIN), and the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines are exploring opportunities to establish a South Korea–Laoag Air Connection, including the possible facilitation of a maiden flight.The familiarization tour also allows Korean travel trade representatives to experience Ilocos Norte’s tourism products, assess its market potential, and establish direct business connections with local tourism stakeholders.The meeting features messages from Hon. Rafael C. Medina and DOT Korea Tourism Attaché Dr. Erwin F. Balane, followed by an Ilocos Norte Tourism Presentation by Aian Raquel of the Ilocos Norte Tourism Office and a Hospitality Investment Presentation by Soya Bueno of the Ilocos Norte Trade and Investment Promotions Office.An open discussion and Business-to-Business Matching session follow, connecting Korean travel trade representatives with local tourism enterprises.The engagement strengthens the PGIN’s efforts to expand its presence in the South Korean market through tourism promotion, potential air connectivity, and direct business partnerships, opening more opportunities for tourism growth and market access in Northern Luzon.

Pre-SOPA Conference reinforces participatory governance in Ilocos Norte

Leading up to Governor Cecilia Araneta-Marcos' inaugural State of the Province Address (SOPA), the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte (PGIN), through the Provincial Information Office, convened representatives from key sectors during the Pre-SOPA Conference to gather sectoral insights and recommendations that will help inform the priorities and key initiatives outlined in the Governor's 2026 State of the Province Address.Serving as a consultative platform, the Pre-SOPA Conference provided representatives from the tourism, entrepreneurship, transportation, youth, and agriculture sectors the opportunity to discuss how provincial government programs have contributed to the development of their respective sectors, identify existing challenges, and present recommendations directly to Governor Araneta-Marcos to help inform the Province's development agenda.Among those who shared their perspectives were Ilokano filmmaker Mr. Harry Turda, who highlighted the Lawag Film Festival's role in promoting Ilocos Norte through film; local entrepreneur Ms. Glenda Tapec, who credited the Producer-to-Consumer Program for helping local businesses expand to wider markets; and transportation representative Mr. Jayrone Agorilla, who emphasized the importance of preserving the Province's kalesa tradition as both a cultural heritage and tourism asset.Meanwhile, youth representative Mr. Josh Rafael Fagaragan underscored the value of leadership development and scholarship programs in preparing young Ilokanos to become active contributors to their communities. Agriculture representative Mr. Freddie Mar Bagaoisan, president of Zanjera Casilian, likewise recognized provincial investments such as the Cold Storage Facility and the Bagsakan Center, which continue to strengthen farmers' livelihoods by improving post-harvest management and expanding market access.Beyond highlighting the gains in their respective sectors, the representatives also presented their sectoral priorities and recommendations directly to Governor Araneta-Marcos. Collectively, their insights reflected a shared aspiration to sustain responsive government programs while pursuing new opportunities to strengthen the Province's economy, empower communities, and improve the quality of life for every Ilokano.The Pre-SOPA Conference reflects PGIN's commitment to participatory governance by ensuring that the perspectives of Ilokanos are heard and considered in shaping the Province's priorities. The insights gathered during the conference will help inform Governor Cecilia Araneta-Marcos' inaugural State of the Province Address on August 3, 2026, reinforcing the administration's commitment to governance that is responsive, inclusive, and grounded in the needs of its people.

August 1, 2026

Over 1,000 Ilocos Norte students receive educational aid

In a significant boost to education support in the province, a total of 1,028 senior high school and college students aged 18 years old and above, all non-recipients of any government scholarship program, each received Php 5,000 in educational assistance to support their continued pursuit of education and help meet school-related expenses.Through a funding request initiated by the Office of the Governor with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), the assistance was provided to qualified students in the province, underscoring the government’s continued effort to support learners who are not covered by existing scholarship programs but are actively pursuing their studies.Governor Cecilia Araneta-Marcos urged the beneficiaries to use the assistance responsibly and prioritize their studies, stressing the value of discipline and perseverance in pursuing their academic goals.For many beneficiaries, the aid provides timely relief for daily academic expenses, transportation, and other school-related needs. Among them is Leriza C. Bonnit, a 3rd year student from Mariano Marcos State University – College of Teacher Education, who expressed gratitude for the support extended to students like her.Meanwhile, Honorable Saul Paulo A. Lazo, Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member and Committee Head on Education, announced that amendments to the Ilocos Norte Scholarship Program are underway to further expand access to educational support across the province.The proposed enhancements include additional scholarship slots and the inclusion of priority courses such as Psychology, Dentistry, and Veterinary Medicine, aimed at broadening opportunities for students pursuing specialized and in-demand professions.The expanded scholarship program has been approved with additional funding by Governor Araneta-Marcos, reinforcing the provincial government’s commitment to strengthening access to higher education and developing a skilled workforce.With these initiatives, immediate educational assistance and long-term scholarship expansion, the Provincial Government continues to reinforce its support for the youth, recognizing education as a key driver of progress in Ilocos Norte.

Ilocos Norte expands global partnerships at Hawai‘i-Philippines Business Symposium

The Ilocos Norte official delegation, headed by Governor Cecilia Araneta-Marcos, expanded international partnerships and advanced cooperation in trade, workforce development, and investment during the 4th Annual Hawai‘i-Philippines Business Tradeshow, Symposium, and Reception held on May 19, which gathered nearly 300 participants from the government, business, and industry sectors.The engagement strengthened the long-standing partnership between the Province of Ilocos Norte and the State of Hawai‘i, which began during the term of then-Governor and now President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and was reinforced during the Ilocos Norte–Hawai‘i Industry Meet-up in 2024. The partnership continues to create opportunities for Ilokanos through sustained economic and cultural cooperation.In the panel discussion “Island Economics in Partnership: Trade, Investment, and Market Access,” Ms. Soya Cheng Bueno, Head of the Ilocos Norte Trade and Investment Promotions Office, highlighted Ilocos Norte’s investment potential and efforts to expand market access for local industries, MSMEs, and tourism enterprises.Meanwhile, Mr. Aianree Raquel, Provincial Tourism Officer, joined the panel of “Workforce, Talent, and Innovation Across Borders,” focusing on workforce development, talent mobility, and innovation-driven collaboration.At the event, Governor Cecilia Araneta-Marcos emphasized the importance of international cooperation in advancing opportunities for Ilokanos and supporting the province’s development agenda.“We value international linkages, particularly with the State of Hawai‘i, to foster investment, knowledge exchange, and business collaboration, opening opportunities in key sectors that generate jobs, support local enterprises, and build a more resilient economy. As we move forward, Ilocos Norte and Hawai‘i remain partners shaped by shared history, working toward stronger economies, empowered communities, and deeper cultural ties. Together, we turn partnership into progress and lasting opportunities for our people.”In line with its development priorities, the Provincial Government continues to champion international linkages that advance key sectors, expand global cooperation, and position Ilocos Norte as a competitive hub for trade, tourism, and innovation. Through sustained engagement with international partners, the province promotes inclusive growth, workforce development, and broader global opportunities for Ilokanos.

Ilokano scholars, youth leaders receive educational assistance

1,794 scholars and youth leaders in Ilocos Norte received educational assistance under the Sirib Provincial Learners Scholarship Program of the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte (PGIN) at Mariano Marcos State University, on May 12.The distribution benefited learners from various scholarship categories, including 818 academic secondary scholars, 148 arts secondary scholars, 651 academic tertiary scholars, 16 Juris Doctor scholars, 15 Doctor of Medicine scholars, 44 technical-vocational scholars, and 102 Sirib youth leaders, reflecting the provincial government’s continued investment in inclusive education for Ilokano learners.Since 2013, PGIN has continued to provide educational assistance established under then Governor and now Senator Imee Marcos, supporting learners through various academic and leadership opportunities. Also, the provincial government institutionalized sector-based support, including the Agri-Fisheries, Law, and Medicine scholarship programs for learners under then Governor Matthew Marcos-Manotoc.Governor Cecilia Araneta-Marcos encouraged scholars to maximize the opportunities provided by the Provincial Government, stating:"This program really is a big help for you and your parents. So, take advantage of this program and make your parents proud because their proudest moment will be you in your graduation."The educational assistance aims to help ease the financial burden of students and their families while encouraging beneficiaries to persevere in their studies and pursue their aspirations.Meanwhile, one of the Juris Doctor beneficiaries, Kristel Janella Baptista, shared that the scholarship is a great help in supporting her studies, saying:“Dakkel a tulong daytoy kanyami nga agbasbasa ti Law. Laguna Board Restores Committee Posts: Agarao Returns to Finance, Gomez Leads Peace and Order
 March 16, 2026
 PIO
English Version
Tagalog Version

Leadership roles in key committees of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Laguna were formally restored today March 16, 2026, following the regular session where Board Member Jam Agarao and Board Member Ardel Gomez were nominated and reinstated to head their respective committees.




Agarao returned as chairperson of the Finance, Budget and Appropriations Committee, while Gomez assumed the role of Chairman of the Peace and Order Committee, reflecting the provincial board’s continued trust in their leadership and commitment to public service.




The development came after Agarao voluntarily stepped down as chairperson of the Peace and Order Committee to ensure that the appointment process strictly follows the procedures stated in the Local Government Code, which require a vacant position, formal nomination, election, and transparency among members of the provincial board.




“Nung nakaraang linggo po, ang inyong lingkod ay natanggal bilang Finance Budget and Appropriations at napa talaga bilang bagong chairman ng Peace and Order. Ako po ay nagreresign bilang committee chairman po ng Peace and Order dahil kailangan po ang pagtatalaga ng bagong chairman ay dumaan sa tamang proseso dahil ito ang nakalagay sa Local Government Code. Kailangan ng vacant seat, nomination, kailangan ng election at kailangan ng transparency para sa mga kasamahan kong Bokal,” Agarao explained during the session.




As part of the process, Agarao nominated Gomez to lead the Peace and Order Committee.

“Bilang respeto po sa dating committee chairman ng Peace and Order, I nominate Bokal Ardel Gomez bilang committee chairman,” she said.




In response, Gomez expressed his appreciation to the majority leaders and presiding officer, and in turn nominated Agarao to return as head of the Finance, Budget and Appropriations Committee.




“Maraming salamat po sa ating majority leaders at presiding officer, naunahan lang po ako. I respectfully nominate our senior board member Jam Agarao for the Finance Budget and Appropriations Committee,” Gomez said.




The nominations were acknowledged during the session, effectively reinstating Agarao and Gomez to their respective committee leadership roles.




Provincial board members noted that the move underscores the body’s commitment to due process, transparency, and cooperation in fulfilling their legislative duties for the people of Laguna.
